stem.text: Measurements are made to determine the activation energy, $E_\text{a}$, of a reaction.
The diagram shows $E_\text{a}$ on the Boltzmann distribution at temperature $T_1$.

stem.alt: Boltzmann distribution graph of number of molecules against energy at T1, with a peak at low energy and E_a marked on the energy axis on the falling tail of the curve.

stem.text: Measurements are then made at a higher temperature, $T_2$.
Which diagram correctly shows the Boltzmann distribution and $E_\text{a}$ at $T_2$?

A.alt: Boltzmann curve of number of molecules against energy with its peak just before E_a, and E_a marked near the peak.

B.alt: Boltzmann curve of number of molecules against energy with its peak to the right of E_a, and E_a marked on the rising part of the curve.

C.alt: Boltzmann curve of number of molecules against energy with its peak to the left of E_a, and E_a marked on the falling tail at a low point.

D.alt: Boltzmann curve of number of molecules against energy with its peak to the left of E_a, and E_a marked on the falling part of the curve.
